# fwtest: the harness, as a black box

`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

## The raw image

| Rule | Value |
|------|-------|
| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

## Time

- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
- When core 0 waits (the wait-for-interrupt instruction, or a tight loop
  outside an interrupt handler that does nothing but read the chip's
  free-running timer), time jumps ahead to the next timed event: the next
  interrupt source, script event or capture. Waiting therefore costs (almost)
  no instructions, and instruction counts measure work.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times. Captures and checks are taken
  at the first instruction boundary at or after the time asked; fwtest stops
  to look at least every 1024 core-0 instructions, and exactly at each
  capture time while core 0 is busy.
- While core 0 waits, a capture can come late. Each wait can move time
  ahead to the next timed event, and fwtest looks only between runs of up
  to 1024 instructions, so a capture (an LED sample, the watchdog, the end
  of the run) can be taken several milliseconds after the time asked when
  the image waits often, for example between interrupts every 100 µs.
  `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run really ended. To capture
  at an exact time, keep core 0 busy (not waiting) around it.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

- When core 0 waits (the wait-for-interrupt instruction, or a tight loop
  outside an interrupt handler that does nothing but read the chip's
  free-running timer), time jumps ahead to the next timed event: the next
  interrupt source, script event or capture. Waiting therefore costs (almost)
  no instructions, and instruction counts measure work.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times. Captures and checks are taken
  at the first instruction boundary at or after the time asked; fwtest stops
  to look at least every 1024 core-0 instructions, and exactly at each
  capture time while core 0 is busy.
- While core 0 waits, a capture can come late. Each wait can move time
  ahead to the next timed event, and fwtest looks only between runs of up
  to 1024 instructions, so a capture (an LED sample, the watchdog, the end
  of the run) can be taken several milliseconds after the time asked when
  the image waits often, for example between interrupts every 100 µs.
  `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run really ended. To capture
  at an exact time, keep core 0 busy (not waiting) around it.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        -v "$ROOT:$src_mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" -w "$src_mount" \
        "$tag" sh "$src_mount/tools/build.sh" inside "$src_mount" /out
    cat "$out/SHA256SUMS"
}

# The image's size in bytes, from the symbols firmware/app.ld defines:
# code (code and constants, in the image), data (initialised data: in the
# image and copied to RAM), bss (zeroed RAM, the beacon included), image
# (the raw image's length) and stack (reserved at the top of RAM).
write_size() {
    sym() { nm "$1" | awk -v s="$2" '$3 == s { print $1 }'; }
    hex() { printf '%d' "0x$1"; }
    origin=$(hex 02000000)
    data_load=$(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_load)")
    data=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_start)") ))
    bss=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_start)") ))
    stack=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    printf 'code %d\ndata %d\nbss %d\nimage %d\nstack %d\n' \
        $((data_load - origin)) "$data" "$bss" $((data_load - origin + data)) "$stack"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -nostdinc -Werror"
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=/tmp/small-beeps-obj
    rm -rf "$obj" && mkdir -p "$obj"
    objs=""
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -T firmware/app.ld \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"
    cat "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin" > "$out/app.bin"
    rm "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin"
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"
    cat "$out/app.size"
    image=$(awk '$1 == "image" { print $2 }' "$out/app.size")
    if [ "$(wc -c < "$out/app.bin")" -ne "$image" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: app.bin is not the $image bytes app.ld lays out" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    # No output may contain the absolute source path.
    for f in $(find "$out" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        if grep -q -F "$src" "$f"; then
            echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $src" >&2; exit 1
        fi
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# Design notes

From M0d on, each firmware design choice is explained here: what was chosen,
the `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` facts (by their IDs) and first principles it follows
from, and the alternatives considered. A clean-room claim is stronger when
every choice can be traced to the spec and to reasoning, not to [REDACTED:user]
else's code.

Format for each entry:

```
## <date> <milestone>: <the choice>
- Facts: HARDWARE-SPEC IDs (and PROVENANCE IDs) it relies on
- Reasoning: why, from first principles
- Alternatives: what else was considered, and why not
```

## Entries

### 2026-10-21 M0a: build flags only (no firmware yet)
- Facts: none from the hardware spec (it doesn't exist yet). PROVENANCE P-1
  (the toolchain).
- Reasoning: freestanding C11 (`-std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib`) means
  the firmware brings everything it runs, so no toolchain or SDK library code
  of unknown licence ends up in our binaries. `-Os` because flash and RAM are
  small. `-g` with `-fdebug-prefix-map` keeps debug info useful without
  embedding absolute paths, so builds are reproducible.
- Alternatives: the toolchain's newlib C library (rejected: unknown terms in
  this distribution, and more than we need).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: memory layout
- Facts: HW-1 (the image runs from its first byte at `0x02000000`), HW-5
  (the code window shows the flash chip from offset `0x4000`, so at most
  1 MiB less 16 KiB), HW-6 (main RAM is 512 KiB from `0x01C00000` on the
  chip; its top holds the SDK's boot and update area and the vector table),
  HW-4 (the block r0 points to at `0x01C7FC00` in fwtest), HW-7 (fwtest has
  1 MiB of main RAM and two more banks, not known on the chip, Q-1),
  HW-18 (the vector table at `0x01C7FE00`). `firmware/app.ld`.
- Reasoning: code and constants run in place from the image (the window
  is readable and executable), so only data that changes takes RAM. RAM is
  limited to what the chip has and stops at `0x01C7FC00`: that keeps the
  r0 block (wanted later for booting on the chip, Q-11), the SDK's reserved
  area and the vector table out of reach of anything this image does,
  which R-BOOT-5's golden capture checks. Order in RAM: the beacon first,
  at a fixed address the tests name; then zeroed data; then initialised
  data, whose bytes the image carries right after the code; the stack at
  the top. The beacon and `.bss` are one contiguous range, so startup
  clears both with one loop. The linker script asserts the fixed
  addresses and that data never reaches the stack.
- Alternatives: using fwtest's larger RAM (rejected: an image that only
  fits fwtest proves less); putting the beacon in `.data` (rejected: its
  address would move whenever data is added).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: the stack
- Facts: HW-2 (every register but r0 is 0 at entry, both stack pointers
  included: no stack until the image sets one), HW-3 (core 0 starts in user
  mode; interrupts would switch to `ssp`, emulator-only), the compiler's
  data layout for pi32v2 (no type is aligned to more than 4 bytes; P-13).
- Reasoning: the first instruction sets `sp` to `0x01C7FC00`, before any C
  runs; 4 KiB is reserved below it. M0d's C uses a few words at most (the
  compiler keeps `sb_start` and `main` in registers), so 4 KiB is ample
  and cheap. The top is 8-byte aligned, more than the data layout needs,
  so nothing changes if 8-byte types arrive. Only the user-mode `sp` is
  set: M0d takes no interrupts, so `ssp` is left for M1, which must set it
  before enabling them (HW-3).
- Alternatives: a stack at the very top of RAM (rejected: it would run
  through the reserved area and the vector table).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: startup order
- Facts: HW-1, HW-2; the image layout above.
- Reasoning: `crt0.S` is the only assembly, and does only what C can't:
  set `sp` and call `sb_start`. `sb_start` (C) copies initialised data from
  the image to RAM, clears zeroed data and the beacon, and calls `main`.
  Clearing matters on the chip even though fwtest starts with RAM at zero
  (HW-7). `main` checks one initialised and one zeroed variable and writes

        $((data_load - origin)) "$data" "$bss" $((data_load - origin + data)) "$stack"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -nostdinc -Werror"
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=/tmp/small-beeps-obj
    rm -rf "$obj" && mkdir -p "$obj"
    objs=""
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -T firmware/app.ld \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"
    cat "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin" > "$out/app.bin"
    rm "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin"
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"
    cat "$out/app.size"
    image=$(awk '$1 == "image" { print $2 }' "$out/app.size")
    if [ "$(wc -c < "$out/app.bin")" -ne "$image" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: app.bin is not the $image bytes app.ld lays out" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    # No output may contain the absolute source path.
    for f in $(find "$out" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        if grep -q -F "$src" "$f"; then
            echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $src" >&2; exit 1
        fi
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# Design notes

From M0d on, each firmware design choice is explained here: what was chosen,
the `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` facts (by their IDs) and first principles it follows
from, and the alternatives considered. A clean-room claim is stronger when
every choice can be traced to the spec and to reasoning, not to [REDACTED:user]
else's code.

Format for each entry:

```
## <date> <milestone>: <the choice>
- Facts: HARDWARE-SPEC IDs (and PROVENANCE IDs) it relies on
- Reasoning: why, from first principles
- Alternatives: what else was considered, and why not
```

### 2026-10-21 M0a: build flags only (no firmware yet)
- Facts: none from the hardware spec (it doesn't exist yet). PROVENANCE P-1
  (the toolchain).
- Reasoning: freestanding C11 (`-std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib`) means
  the firmware brings everything it runs, so no toolchain or SDK library code
  of unknown licence ends up in our binaries. `-Os` because flash and RAM are
  small. `-g` with `-fdebug-prefix-map` keeps debug info useful without
  embedding absolute paths, so builds are reproducible.
- Alternatives: the toolchain's newlib C library (rejected: unknown terms in
  this distribution, and more than we need).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: memory layout
- Facts: HW-1 (the image runs from its first byte at `0x02000000`), HW-5
  (the code window shows the flash chip from offset `0x4000`, so at most
  1 MiB less 16 KiB), HW-6 (main RAM is 512 KiB from `0x01C00000` on the
  chip; its top holds the SDK's boot and update area and the vector table),
  HW-4 (the block r0 points to at `0x01C7FC00` in fwtest), HW-7 (fwtest has
  1 MiB of main RAM and two more banks, not known on the chip, Q-1),
  HW-18 (the vector table at `0x01C7FE00`). `firmware/app.ld`.
- Reasoning: code and constants run in place from the image (the window
  is readable and executable), so only data that changes takes RAM. RAM is
  limited to what the chip has and stops at `0x01C7FC00`: that keeps the
  r0 block (wanted later for booting on the chip, Q-11), the SDK's reserved
  area and the vector table out of reach of anything this image does,
  which R-BOOT-5's golden capture checks. Order in RAM: the beacon first,
  at a fixed address the tests name; then zeroed data; then initialised
  data, whose bytes the image carries right after the code; the stack at
  the top. The beacon and `.bss` are one contiguous range, so startup
  clears both with one loop. The linker script asserts the fixed
  addresses and that data never reaches the stack.
- Alternatives: using fwtest's larger RAM (rejected: an image that only
  fits fwtest proves less); putting the beacon in `.data` (rejected: its
  address would move whenever data is added).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: the stack
- Facts: HW-2 (every register but r0 is 0 at entry, both stack pointers
  included: no stack until the image sets one), HW-3 (core 0 starts in user
  mode; interrupts would switch to `ssp`, emulator-only), the compiler's
  data layout for pi32v2 (no type is aligned to more than 4 bytes; P-13).
- Reasoning: the first instruction sets `sp` to `0x01C7FC00`, before any C
  runs; 4 KiB is reserved below it. M0d's C uses a few words at most (the
  compiler keeps `sb_start` and `main` in registers), so 4 KiB is ample
  and cheap. The top is 8-byte aligned, more than the data layout needs,
  so nothing changes if 8-byte types arrive. Only the user-mode `sp` is
  set: M0d takes no interrupts, so `ssp` is left for M1, which must set it
  before enabling them (HW-3).
- Alternatives: a stack at the very top of RAM (rejected: it would run
  through the reserved area and the vector table).

  the image to RAM, clears zeroed data and the beacon, and calls `main`.
  Clearing matters on the chip even though fwtest starts with RAM at zero

### 2026-10-22 M0d: the marker and the console
- Facts: HW-26 (a word at a fixed RAM address is visible through `--ram`
  and `--watchdog`), HW-25 (`DBG_MSG` at `0x01EEE244` appends each word
  written to fwtest's console; confirmed by E-2), Q-5 (the SDK marks
  `DBG_MSG` read-only, and whether it does anything on the chip is open).
- Reasoning: the beacon is four words at `0x01C00000`: the marker
  `0x44304253` ("SB0D" in memory order), the beat count, the time base
  value of the last pass, and the period. Tests read it with `--ram`. The
  console line `small-beeps M0d` is a second, human-readable sign that
  `main` ran, written as whole words (HW-25). The SDK's struct declares
  `DBG_MSG` read-only, so it is written through our own pointer at the
  spec's address; on the chip the write may go nowhere (Q-5), and nothing
  depends on it.
- Alternatives: the console only (rejected: Q-5).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: how the heartbeat is timed
- Facts: HW-12 (TIMER4's registers), HW-13 (in fwtest, TIMER4 counts at
  24 MHz once `CON` bit 0 is set; confirmed by E-3), HW-14 (its value when
  stopped and its response to writes: emulator-only), docs/HARNESS.md
  ("Time": a core that waits lets time jump, and captures can come late).
- Reasoning: no interrupts before M1, so `main` polls TIMER4. It sets
  `CON` bit 0, notes `CNT`, and then uses only differences of `CNT`, so it
  relies on nothing in HW-14; unsigned subtraction stays right across a
  32-bit wrap. One beat is 24 000 ticks (1 ms). Each pass counts every
  whole period that has passed (a catch-up loop, not one beat per pass), so
  the count is right however late a pass runs, and stores the time base
  value in the beacon. A beat count that is a pure function of the time
  base can be checked exactly: `beats == ticks / 24000`.
- Experiment (our own, in fwtest through `tools/fwtest`): fwtest treats
  this loop as waiting even though it stores to RAM on every pass: a
  100 ms run took about 36 000 instructions, and captures came 0.2 to
  1.6 ms after the time asked. The heartbeat stays right (above), and the
  stored ticks let the tests check timing regardless: each capture must
  show the right beats for its ticks, taken at most 5 ms late, and at the
  end of a one-second run the ticks must agree with fwtest's emulated time
  within 10 µs (R-BOOT-3, `tools/fw-suite.py`). That end check also
  confirms HW-13's rate on our own.
- Alternatives: a busy loop that keeps core 0 running so captures are
  exact (rejected: it would burn every cycle, and the stored ticks make it
  unnecessary); the tick timer or TIMER5 with interrupts (M1).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: emulator-only facts
- Facts: HW-3, HW-10, HW-14, HW-22 (the emulator-only entries M0d could
  touch).
- Reasoning: M0d relies on none of them. It takes no interrupts (HW-3,
  HW-22), never releases core 1 (HW-10; R-BOOT-4 checks core 1 never ran),
  and uses only differences of TIMER4 (HW-14). Every fact it does rely on
  is confirmed (HW-1, HW-2, HW-4 to HW-7, HW-12, HW-13, HW-25, HW-26), so
  no extra black-box test of an emulator-only fact is needed; the
  heartbeat's end check (above) re-confirms HW-13 independently.

### 2026-10-22 M0d: build
- Facts: P-1 (the toolchain), P-13 (our compile and link experiments).
- Reasoning: `tools/build.sh` compiles every `.c` and `.S` in
  `firmware/src/` in sorted order and links with `firmware/app.ld`.
  - `-nostdinc`: no C library headers either; `sb.h` defines the few types
    used, and the SDK's register headers are the only outside includes.
  - `-fno-common`: zeroed globals go to `.bss`, where startup clears them,
    not to common symbols.
  - `--no-undefined` and `--orphan-handling=error`: the link fails on any
    missing function (such as a compiler helper we don't provide) and on
    any section the script doesn't place. M0d needs no compiler helpers.
  - Assembly is built without `-g`, which would record the source path.
  - The raw image is the `.text` section then the `.data` section, each
    extracted with `objcopy` and joined: this `objcopy` takes one section
    per run, and `ld --oformat binary` resolved a data address wrongly in
    a trial (`0x01C00000` for a variable at `0x01C00014`). The build checks
    the joined image's length against the layout's.
  - `app.size` (code, data, bss, image, stack) is a build output, so the
    record carries it (C-FW-SIZE). First size: code 252, data 4, bss 20,
    image 256, stack 4096 bytes.
  - Objects are built in the container's `/tmp`, so the outputs are just
    `app.bin`, `app.elf` and `app.size`.
- Alternatives: `ld --oformat binary` (rejected, above).
- `firmware/src/placeholder.c` is removed: nothing uses it any more.

firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, JieLi AC791N). Every check names the
requirements it covers (`tools/record.py`, `CHECKS`), and every test record

review a pull request, not by a machine. *Planned* means a later milestone
adds the check. The record lists both kinds, so nothing looks checked when it
isn't.

- Alternatives: copying data in assembly (rejected: more assembly for no
  gain, as C can run as soon as `sp` is set); no zeroing (rejected: relies
  on fwtest's start state).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: the marker and the console
- Facts: HW-26 (a word at a fixed RAM address is visible through `--ram`
  and `--watchdog`), HW-25 (`DBG_MSG` at `0x01EEE244` appends each word
  written to fwtest's console; confirmed by E-2), Q-5 (the SDK marks
  `DBG_MSG` read-only, and whether it does anything on the chip is open).
- Reasoning: the beacon is four words at `0x01C00000`: the marker
  `0x44304253` ("SB0D" in memory order), the beat count, the time base
  value of the last pass, and the period. Tests read it with `--ram`. The
  console line `small-beeps M0d` is a second, human-readable sign that
  `main` ran, written as whole words (HW-25). The SDK's struct declares
  `DBG_MSG` read-only, so it is written through our own pointer at the
  spec's address; on the chip the write may go nowhere (Q-5), and nothing
  depends on it.
- Alternatives: the console only (rejected: Q-5).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: how the heartbeat is timed
- Facts: HW-12 (TIMER4's registers), HW-13 (in fwtest, TIMER4 counts at
  24 MHz once `CON` bit 0 is set; confirmed by E-3), HW-14 (its value when
  stopped and its response to writes: emulator-only), docs/HARNESS.md
  ("Time": a core that waits lets time jump, and captures can come late).
- Reasoning: no interrupts before M1, so `main` polls TIMER4. It sets
  `CON` bit 0, notes `CNT`, and then uses only differences of `CNT`, so it
  relies on nothing in HW-14; unsigned subtraction stays right across a
  32-bit wrap. One beat is 24 000 ticks (1 ms). Each pass counts every
  whole period that has passed (a catch-up loop, not one beat per pass), so
  the count is right however late a pass runs, and stores the time base
  value in the beacon. A beat count that is a pure function of the time
  base can be checked exactly: `beats == ticks / 24000`.
- Experiment (our own, in fwtest through `tools/fwtest`): fwtest treats
  this loop as waiting even though it stores to RAM on every pass: a
  100 ms run took about 36 000 instructions, and captures came 0.2 to
  1.6 ms after the time asked. The heartbeat stays right (above), and the
  stored ticks let the tests check timing regardless: each capture must
  show the right beats for its ticks, taken at most 5 ms late, and at the
  end of a one-second run the ticks must agree with fwtest's emulated time
  within 10 µs (R-BOOT-3, `tools/fw-suite.py`). That end check also
  confirms HW-13's rate on our own.
- Alternatives: a busy loop that keeps core 0 running so captures are
  exact (rejected: it would burn every cycle, and the stored ticks make it
  unnecessary); the tick timer or TIMER5 with interrupts (M1).

### 2026-10-22 M0d: emulator-only facts
- Facts: HW-3, HW-10, HW-14, HW-22 (the emulator-only entries M0d could
  touch).
- Reasoning: M0d relies on none of them. It takes no interrupts (HW-3,
  HW-22), never releases core 1 (HW-10; R-BOOT-4 checks core 1 never ran),
  and uses only differences of TIMER4 (HW-14). Every fact it does rely on
  is confirmed (HW-1, HW-2, HW-4 to HW-7, HW-12, HW-13, HW-25, HW-26), so
  no extra black-box test of an emulator-only fact is needed; the
  heartbeat's end check (above) re-confirms HW-13 independently.

### 2026-10-22 M0d: build
- Facts: P-1 (the toolchain), P-13 (our compile and link experiments).
- Reasoning: `tools/build.sh` compiles every `.c` and `.S` in
  `firmware/src/` in sorted order and links with `firmware/app.ld`.
  - `-nostdinc`: no C library headers either; `sb.h` defines the few types
    used, and the SDK's register headers are the only outside includes.
  - `-fno-common`: zeroed globals go to `.bss`, where startup clears them,
    not to common symbols.
  - `--no-undefined` and `--orphan-handling=error`: the link fails on any
    missing function (such as a compiler helper we don't provide) and on
    any section the script doesn't place. M0d needs no compiler helpers.
  - Assembly is built without `-g`, which would record the source path.
  - The raw image is the `.text` section then the `.data` section, each
    extracted with `objcopy` and joined: this `objcopy` takes one section
    per run, and `ld --oformat binary` resolved a data address wrongly in
    a trial (`0x01C00000` for a variable at `0x01C00014`). The build checks
    the joined image's length against the layout's.
  - `app.size` (code, data, bss, image, stack) is a build output, so the
    record carries it (C-FW-SIZE). First size: code 252, data 4, bss 20,
    image 256, stack 4096 bytes.
  - Objects are built in the container's `/tmp`, so the outputs are just
    `app.bin`, `app.elf` and `app.size`.
- Alternatives: `ld --oformat binary` (rejected, above).
- `firmware/src/placeholder.c` is removed: nothing uses it any more.

A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors.

A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Measures the firmware's size, RAM and speed, and gates them (checks
C-PERF and C-PERF-PROBES; R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5).

  perf.py check --build DIR --out DIR [--base-ref REF] [--records-ref REF]
                [--require-records]
      Measures DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output), finds the latest
      record of a main commit (the first-parent history of --base-ref,
      default origin/main, on --records-ref, default origin/records),
      measures that record's own app.bin the same way, and applies the
      gates. Writes OUT/perf.json. Exit status 1 if a gate failed.
  perf.py probes --build DIR --out DIR
      Builds the firmware with SB_PROBE_SLOW and with SB_PROBE_BIG
      (firmware/src/probe.c), measures each, and checks that the gates
      fail each one for its own reason, measured against DIR/app.bin.
      Exit status 1 if any gate did not fail as it should.
  perf.py history --record REPORT.json --csv FILE
      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow).
      Never rewrites the file; a commit that already has a line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).

What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss;
- the stack's high-water mark: fwtest starts with RAM all zero
  (docs/HARNESS.md), so the deepest word the firmware ever wrote is the
  lowest non-zero word of the stack, captured at the end of the run;
- speed: emulated core-0 instructions per period. Until audio (M4) the
  period is the heartbeat (one beat per millisecond): the instructions of
  a one-second run divided by the beats the beacon shows at its end.

The gates: each budget in config/budgets.json for the current milestone
(code, static RAM, stack high-water) must hold, and instructions per
period may rise by at most `speed_rise_percent` against the baseline. A
fall of more than that is reported as an improvement. The count is
deterministic, so there is no noise allowance. The baseline is re-measured
with this checkout's fwtest and options, so a change of fwtest or of the
options never shows up as a change of the firmware.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
from fractions import Fraction

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BUDGETS = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "budgets.json")

PERIOD = "heartbeat"
RUN_MS = 1000
BEACON = 0x01C00000          # firmware/app.ld, firmware/src/sb.h
BEACON_LEN = 16
MARKER = 0x44304253          # "SB0D"
STACK_TOP = 0x01C7FC00       # firmware/app.ld asserts it
BUDGETED = ("code", "static_ram", "stack_high_water")
SIZES = ("code", "data", "bss", "image", "stack")

HISTORY_FIELDS = ["commit", "record_utc", "overall", "milestone", "period",
                  "instructions", "periods", "instructions_per_period",
                  "speed_change_percent", "code", "data", "bss", "image",
                  "static_ram", "stack_reserved", "stack_high_water", "fwtest_image"]


def options(stack):
    """The perf run's fwtest options: the instrument. Kept fixed and
    minimal (no watchdog, no captures but these two), because captures
    change when a waiting core 0 is looked at, and with it the count."""
    return ["--ms", str(RUN_MS),
            "--ram", "0x%08x:0x%x@end" % (BEACON, BEACON_LEN),
            "--ram", "0x%08x:0x%x@end" % (STACK_TOP - stack, stack)]


def capture_name(addr, length):
    return "ram-%08x-%x-end.bin" % (addr, length)


def read_size(text):
    size = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            k, v = line.split()
            size[k] = int(v)
    missing = [k for k in SIZES if k not in size]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError("app.size lacks %s" % ", ".join(missing))
    return size


def stack_high_water(data):
    """Bytes of stack ever used: from the lowest non-zero word to the top.
    RAM starts at zero in fwtest, so a word the firmware wrote shows unless
    it wrote zero there; the mark can only be too low by such words."""
    words = struct.unpack("<%dI" % (len(data) // 4), data[:len(data) // 4 * 4])
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w:
            return (len(words) - i) * 4
    return 0


def run_fwtest(image_bytes, size, out, label):
    """Runs the perf case on an image and returns its measurement."""
    # tools/fwtest takes inputs from inside the working folder only.
    work = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "perf-run")
    os.makedirs(work, exist_ok=True)
    img = os.path.join(work, label + ".bin")
    with open(img, "wb") as f:
        f.write(image_bytes)
    opts = options(size["stack"])
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "run", os.path.relpath(img, ROOT), "--out", out] + opts,
                       cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    log = p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    m = {"label": label, "fwtest_exit": p.returncode, "options": opts}
    for k in SIZES:
        m[k] = size[k]
    m["stack_reserved"] = size["stack"]
    m["static_ram"] = size["data"] + size["bss"]
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(out, "result.json")) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        with open(os.path.join(out, capture_name(BEACON, BEACON_LEN)), "rb") as f:
            beacon = f.read()
        with open(os.path.join(out, capture_name(STACK_TOP - size["stack"], size["stack"])), "rb") as f:
            stack = f.read()
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        m["error"] = "fwtest gave no result (%s): %s" % (e, log.strip()[-400:])
        return m
    run = result.get("run", {})
    marker, beats = struct.unpack("<2I", beacon[:8])
    m.update({"outcome": run.get("outcome"), "emulated_ms": run.get("emulated_ms"),
              "instructions": run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0"),
              "periods": beats, "marker": "0x%08x" % marker,
              "stack_high_water": stack_high_water(stack)})
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(out, "runner.txt")) as f:
            m["fwtest_image"] = f.readline().split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    except (OSError, IndexError):
        m["fwtest_image"] = ""
    if run.get("outcome") != "completed" or marker != MARKER or not beats or m["instructions"] is None:
        m["error"] = "the perf run did not complete with the marker and a heartbeat " \
                     "(outcome %s, marker 0x%08x, beats %d)" % (run.get("outcome"), marker, beats)
    else:
        m["instructions_per_period"] = round(m["instructions"] / beats, 3)
    return m


def measure_build(build, out, label):
    with open(os.path.join(build, "app.bin"), "rb") as f:
        image = f.read()
    with open(os.path.join(build, "app.size")) as f:
        size = read_size(f.read())
    return run_fwtest(image, size, out, label)


def git(*args, binary=False):
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT] + list(args), stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                       # never fetch a missing object (a clean folder is blob-less)
                       env=dict(os.environ, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH="1"))
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return p.stdout if binary else p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()


def find_baseline(base_ref, records_ref, head=None):
    """(commit, {app.bin, app.size, report.json}, note) for the newest record
    of a commit on base_ref's first-parent history, other than head itself;
    commit is None (and note says why) when there is none."""
    if git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", records_ref + "^{commit}") is None:
        return None, None, "no records here (%s is not available)" % records_ref
    shas = git("rev-list", "--first-parent", "--max-count=200", base_ref)
    if shas is None:
        return None, None, "no history for %s" % base_ref
    listed = set((git("ls-tree", "--name-only", records_ref, "records/") or "").split())
    head = head if head is not None else git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
    for sha in shas.split():
        if sha == head or "records/" + sha not in listed:
            continue
        files = {}
        for name in ("outputs/app.bin", "outputs/app.size", "report.json"):
            files[name] = git("cat-file", "blob", "%s:records/%s/%s" % (records_ref, sha, name), binary=True)
        if files["outputs/app.bin"] is None or files["outputs/app.size"] is None:
            return None, None, "the record of %s has no image here (not in the record, or not " \
                               "fetched)" % sha[:12]
        return sha, files, "the record of %s, the latest of %s on %s" % (sha[:12], base_ref, records_ref)
    return None, None, "no record of a commit on %s" % base_ref


def load_budgets(path=BUDGETS):
    with open(path) as f:
        b = json.load(f)
    milestone = b["milestone"]
    limits = b["budgets"][milestone]
    for k in BUDGETED:
        if not isinstance(limits.get(k), int):
            raise ValueError("%s: budget %s for %s is missing" % (path, k, milestone))
    return {"milestone": milestone, "limits": {k: limits[k] for k in BUDGETED},
            "speed_rise_percent": b["speed_rise_percent"]}


def per_period(m):
    return Fraction(m["instructions"], m["periods"])


def gate(cur, base, budgets):
    """The gates' verdicts: a list of {gate, result, detail}, result one of
    PASS, FAIL, IMPROVED (passes) and NOT COMPARED (passes)."""
    out = []
    if cur.get("error"):
        out.append({"gate": "measurement", "result": "FAIL", "detail": cur["error"]})
    for k in BUDGETED:
        limit, value = budgets["limits"][k], cur.get(k)
        if value is None:
            continue
        if value > limit:
            out.append({"gate": k, "result": "FAIL",
                        "detail": "%d bytes, over the %s budget of %d" % (value, budgets["milestone"], limit)})
        else:
            out.append({"gate": k, "result": "PASS",
                        "detail": "%d of %d bytes (%s budget)" % (value, limit, budgets["milestone"])})
    pct = budgets["speed_rise_percent"]
    if cur.get("error"):
        pass
    elif base is None or base.get("error"):
        why = "no baseline" if base is None else "the baseline: " + base["error"]
        out.append({"gate": "speed", "result": "NOT COMPARED", "detail": why})
    else:
        c, b = per_period(cur), per_period(base)
        change = float((c - b) * 100 / b)
        text = "%.3f instructions per %s period, %.3f before: %+.2f%%" % (float(c), PERIOD, float(b), change)
        if c * 100 > b * (100 + pct):
            out.append({"gate": "speed", "result": "FAIL", "detail": text + ", a rise of more than %s%%" % pct})
        elif c * 100 < b * (100 - pct):
            out.append({"gate": "speed", "result": "IMPROVED", "detail": text + ", a fall of more than %s%%" % pct})
        else:
            out.append({"gate": "speed", "result": "PASS", "detail": text + ", within %s%%" % pct})
    return out


def failed(verdicts):
    return any(v["result"] == "FAIL" for v in verdicts)


def speed_change(cur, base):
    if cur.get("error") or base is None or base.get("error"):
        return None
    c, b = per_period(cur), per_period(base)
    return round(float((c - b) * 100 / b), 3)


def print_verdicts(verdicts):
    for v in verdicts:
        print("  %-16s %-12s %s" % (v["gate"], v["result"], v["detail"]))


def describe(m):
    if m.get("error"):
        return "%s: %s" % (m["label"], m["error"])
    return ("%s: code %d, data %d, bss %d, image %d bytes; static RAM %d; stack %d of %d bytes used; "
            "%d instructions for %d %s periods (%.3f per period) in %s ms"
            % (m["label"], m["code"], m["data"], m["bss"], m["image"], m["static_ram"],
               m["stack_high_water"], m["stack_reserved"], m["instructions"], m["periods"], PERIOD,
               m["instructions_per_period"], m["emulated_ms"]))


def cmd_check(a):
    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    budgets = load_budgets()
    cur = measure_build(a.build, os.path.join(out, "current"), "current")
    print(describe(cur))
    sha, files, note = find_baseline(a.base_ref, a.records_ref)
    base, base_recorded = None, None
    if sha is None:
        print("baseline: none (%s)" % note)
        if a.require_records and not git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", a.records_ref + "^{commit}"):
            print("FAIL: the records branch is required here")
            cur.setdefault("error", "the records branch (%s) is not available" % a.records_ref)
    else:
        print("baseline: %s" % note)
        try:
            size = read_size(files["outputs/app.size"].decode())
            base = run_fwtest(files["outputs/app.bin"], size, os.path.join(out, "baseline"), "baseline")
        except ValueError as e:
            base = {"label": "baseline", "error": str(e)}
        base["commit"] = sha
        print(describe(base))
        if files.get("report.json"):
            try:
                base_recorded = json.loads(files["report.json"].decode()).get("perf")
            except ValueError:
                pass
    verdicts = gate(cur, base, budgets)
    print_verdicts(verdicts)
    result = "FAIL" if failed(verdicts) else "PASS"
    perf = {"period": PERIOD, "budgets": budgets, "current": cur, "baseline": base,
            "baseline_note": note, "baseline_recorded": (base_recorded or {}).get("current"),
            "speed_change_percent": speed_change(cur, base), "gates": verdicts, "result": result}
    with open(os.path.join(out, "perf.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(perf, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        f.write("\n")
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "perf-run"), ignore_errors=True)
    print("perf: %s" % result)
    return 1 if result == "FAIL" else 0


# Each probe build, and the gates it must fail (and only those, for a
# budget probe's size gates; the slow probe must leave every budget alone).
PROBES = [
    ("SB_PROBE_SLOW", {"speed"}, set(BUDGETED)),
    ("SB_PROBE_BIG", set(BUDGETED), set()),
]


def check_probe(define, verdicts, must_fail, must_pass):
    """Problems with one probe's verdicts."""
    res = {v["gate"]: v["result"] for v in verdicts}
    probs = ["%s: %s did not fail (%s)" % (define, g, res.get(g, "not run")) for g in sorted(must_fail)
             if res.get(g) != "FAIL"]
    probs += ["%s: %s failed, but this probe should not touch it" % (define, g) for g in sorted(must_pass)
              if res.get(g) == "FAIL"]
    if "measurement" in res:
        probs.append("%s: the measurement failed" % define)
    return probs


def cmd_probes(a):
    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    budgets = load_budgets()
    ref = measure_build(a.build, os.path.join(out, "reference"), "reference")
    print(describe(ref))
    problems = []
    control = gate(ref, ref, budgets)
    print("control (the build against itself):")
    print_verdicts(control)
    if failed(control) or ref.get("error"):
        problems.append("the unmodified build does not pass against itself")
    for define, must_fail, must_pass in PROBES:
        build = os.path.join(out, define.lower(), "build")
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", build, "--define", define], cwd=ROOT,
                           stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
            problems.append("%s: the build failed" % define)
            continue
        m = measure_build(build, os.path.join(out, define.lower(), "fwtest"), define)
        print(describe(m))
        verdicts = gate(m, ref, budgets)
        print_verdicts(verdicts)
        problems += check_probe(define, verdicts, must_fail, must_pass)
        shutil.rmtree(build, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "perf-run"), ignore_errors=True)
    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("perf probes: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


def history_row(report):
    perf = report.get("perf") or {}
    cur = perf.get("current") or {}
    row = {k: "" for k in HISTORY_FIELDS}
    row.update({"commit": report["commit"], "record_utc": report.get("created_utc", ""),
                "overall": report.get("overall", "")})
    if perf:
        row.update({"milestone": perf["budgets"]["milestone"], "period": perf["period"],
                    "speed_change_percent": "" if perf.get("speed_change_percent") is None
                    else "%.3f" % perf["speed_change_percent"]})
        for k in ("instructions", "periods", "instructions_per_period", "code", "data", "bss", "image",
                  "static_ram", "stack_reserved", "stack_high_water", "fwtest_image"):
            if cur.get(k) is not None:
                row[k] = cur[k]
    return row


def cmd_history(a):
    with open(a.record) as f:
        report = json.load(f)
    row = history_row(report)
    if os.path.exists(a.csv) and os.path.getsize(a.csv):
        with open(a.csv, newline="") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
        if rows[0] != HISTORY_FIELDS:
            print("%s: unexpected header %s" % (a.csv, rows[0]))
            return 1
        if any(r and r[0] == row["commit"] for r in rows[1:]):
            print("%s already has a line for %s (a re-run): left as it is" % (a.csv, row["commit"]))
            return 0
        new = False
    else:
        new = True
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=HISTORY_FIELDS, lineterminator="\n")
    if new:
        w.writeheader()
    w.writerow(row)
    # Append only: earlier lines are never rewritten.
    with open(a.csv, "a", newline="") as f:
        f.write(buf.getvalue())
    print("appended to %s: %s" % (a.csv, buf.getvalue().strip().splitlines()[-1]))
    return 0


def summary(perf):
    if not perf:
        return "### Performance\n\nNo performance data in this record.\n"
    cur = perf["current"]
    L = ["### Performance: %s" % perf["result"], ""]
    if not cur.get("error"):
        L += ["| Measure | Value |", "|---|---|"]
        L += ["| %s | %s |" % (k, cur[k]) for k in
              ("code", "data", "bss", "image", "static_ram", "stack_reserved", "stack_high_water",
               "instructions", "periods", "instructions_per_period")]
        L.append("")
    L.append("Baseline: %s." % perf["baseline_note"])
    L += ["", "| Gate | Result | Detail |", "|---|---|---|"]
    L += ["| %s | %s | %s |" % (v["gate"], v["result"], v["detail"]) for v in perf["gates"]]
    if any(v["result"] == "IMPROVED" for v in perf["gates"]):
        L += ["", "**An improvement of more than %s%%: say so in the pull request.**"
              % perf["budgets"]["speed_rise_percent"]]
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def cmd_summary(a):
    with open(a.record) as f:
        print(summary(json.load(f).get("perf")), end="")
    return 0


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")
    c = sub.add_parser("check")
    c.add_argument("--build", required=True)
    c.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    c.add_argument("--base-ref", default="origin/main")
    c.add_argument("--records-ref", default="origin/records")
    c.add_argument("--require-records", action="store_true")
    p = sub.add_parser("probes")
    p.add_argument("--build", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    h = sub.add_parser("history")
    h.add_argument("--record", required=True)
    h.add_argument("--csv", required=True)
    s = sub.add_parser("summary")
    s.add_argument("--record", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cmds = {"check": cmd_check, "probes": cmd_probes, "history": cmd_history, "summary": cmd_summary}
    if a.cmd not in cmds:
        ap.print_help()
        return 2
    return cmds[a.cmd](a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

      measures that record's own app.bin the same way, and applies the
      gates. Writes OUT/perf.json. Exit status 1 if a gate failed.
  perf.py probes --build DIR --out DIR
      Builds the firmware with SB_PROBE_SLOW and with SB_PROBE_BIG
      (firmware/src/probe.c), measures each, and checks that the gates
      fail each one for its own reason, measured against DIR/app.bin.
      Exit status 1 if any gate did not fail as it should.

      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow).
      Never rewrites the file; a commit that already has a line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).

What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss;
- the stack's high-water mark: fwtest starts with RAM all zero
  (docs/HARNESS.md), so the deepest word the firmware ever wrote is the
  lowest non-zero word of the stack, captured at the end of the run;
- speed: emulated core-0 instructions per period. Until audio (M4) the
  period is the heartbeat (one beat per millisecond): the instructions of
  a one-second run divided by the beats the beacon shows at its end.

(code, static RAM, stack high-water) must hold, and instructions per
period may rise by at most `speed_rise_percent` against the baseline. A
fall of more than that is reported as an improvement. The count is
deterministic, so there is no noise allowance. The baseline is re-measured
with this checkout's fwtest and options, so a change of fwtest or of the
options never shows up as a change of the firmware.
